title: How busy is too busy?
hook: How busy is too busy? Change one condition and inspect the result.

knows: that a toy model states its assumptions
doesNotKnow: set arrival and service rates; customers animate in, and the line explodes as utilization nears 100%.

misconception: A toy M/M/1 queue serves 10 people/hour. Arrivals increase from 5 to 8/hour. What is the long-run mean number in the system at 8/hour? The prediction alternatives contrast different consequences of the stated model.

claims.text: A toy M/M/1 queue serves 10 people/hour. Arrivals increase from 5 to 8/hour. What is the long-run mean number in the system at 8/hour? Options: 2; 4; 8. Toy model: compare two controlled cases.
claims.source: Stipulated numerical case in model.ts, based on manager numericCase: M/M/1 hypothetical arrivallambda and serviceratemu=10/hour; lambda5,8,9 givesutilization.5,.8,.9 and meanL=rho/(1-rho)=1,4,9. Never useformulaatlambda>=mu; show unstable.

claims.text: A matching queue serves 12/hour and receives 6/hour. What is the mean number in the system? ρ=1/2, so ρ/(1−ρ)=1.

claims.text: At 8 arrivals/hour, the retained mean is 4 people; at 9/hour it is 9. The service rate stays 10/hour.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-coffee-shop-queue/model.ts#compute().reveal[0]; stipulated local model, independent verification pending.

claims.text: The toy M/M/1 formula is ρ/(1−ρ), with Poisson arrivals, independent exponential service and one server. Approaching full utilization makes the mean grow nonlinearly; this formula applies only below capacity.
